clue.text: Wet stain shrinking

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or blemish, as a stain does
shrinking as in timid, retiring

explanation.surface: A wet stain that shrinks as it dries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stain' reads as a noun but works as the verb MAR, and 'shrinking' is the shy kind, not the drying kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is boggy and waterlogged, so wet is a straightforward synonym for this adjective.

clue.text: Simplest forms requiring an editor?

explanation.definitionFit: Copy full of spelling mistakes needs correcting, which is exactly an editor's job, so the description is fair if indirect.

clue.text: Priest has installed a device using atomic energy

taken as written

explanation.surface: A vicar has had a nuclear gadget fitted in the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: A rector, the parish priest in the Church of England, takes in the single letter after his second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the plant that harnesses fission, the device that turns atomic energy into usable heat and power.

clue.text: Sit on reverse in car

blocks.note: a bird sits on eggs to hatch them
to reverse a vehicle is to back it

explanation.surface: Driving lessons: sitting in the car and putting it into reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit on' suggests a driver's seat, but it is a brooding hen; 'reverse' is not a turnaround signal here but a plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a style of car with a rear door hinged at the roof, opening onto the boot.

explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel, historically prized for its speed, so the description fits.

clue.text: Firework each winter turned on end

explanation.surface: Every winter a firework is set off standing on its end.

explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a pinned spinning firework, named after the saint martyred on a wheel, so it is an example.

clue.text: Board requiring agreement from two countries?

explanation.surface: A company board can only act once two nations both sign off.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is not a committee but the lettered séance board, whose name joins the French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a spiritualist's lettered board used to spell out supposed messages from the dead.

clue.text: Island capital, one island I found in North America

the Roman numeral for one

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: N and A wrap round the middle trio; Cos is also spelt Kos, and gives the cos lettuce its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, a Mediterranean island nation, so it is an example of the class.

clue.text: Some creatures I’d exported, live

explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' sounds like an adjective about the creatures, but it is the verb as in dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there, so the verb live is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Phoney sent in, cries out for medical expert

blocks.note: taken as written, fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: When a fake is brought in as a specialist, the public cries out in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like part of the phrase 'cries out', but its letters are needed in the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuroscientist studies the brain and nervous system, a scientific specialist whose work underpins medicine.

clue.text: Recollection of cattiness, most brief

indicators.note: read as re-collection, gathering the letters again into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Remembering someone's spiteful remark, cut as short as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollection' means memory on the surface, but split as re-collection it means gathering the letters up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means barely sufficient or skimpy, so the superlative describes the shortest, most meagre amount, matching briefest.

clue.text: Home cut method of payment for old people

indicators.note: something cut has been trimmed short, so the last letter is lopped off

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
paying in notes and coins

explanation.surface: Pensioners at home find their payment method reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' suggests pensioners, but it means an ancient people, a civilisation of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were a pre-Columbian civilisation of the Andes, a historical nation, so they count as a people of long ago.

clue.text: Jug painting under discussion?

explanation.surface: A painting of a jug is being debated by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words match only in loose speech, which the question mark concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large vessel with a handle and lip for pouring liquids, the same object as a jug.

clue.text: Dodgy pedals on bicycle finally went

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Faulty pedals on a bike eventually gave out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' tempts as the end of the story, broke down, but it means time went by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by, so the past tense went fits, as in hours went by.

clue.text: Girl fed starter of vegetarian grub

blocks.note: a girl's name
the first letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like slang for food, matching the meal picture, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature wingless stage of an insect, and a grub is the common name for a beetle's larva.

clue.text: Swimmer in shade in Florida, extremely sunburnt earlier

clue.text: Dog enraged at barking

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant German breed, so it is a specific example of the general class of dogs.

clue.text: Pressure on item, something very small

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an article is an item, as in an article of clothing

explanation.surface: Pressure applied to an object until it is reduced to something tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so P sits at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute portion of matter, such as a speck of dust, so the phrase describes it well.

clue.text: Reduce team where loads taken off

blocks.note: to dock pay is to reduce it
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Cutting a squad to lighten the burden it carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken off' echoes the reducing idea, but here it means cargo unloaded from a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are unloaded at the quay beside the dock, so this describes the place where cargo comes ashore.

clue.text: Direct lines into Odense after evacuation

indicators.note: an evacuated building has been cleared out, so the inside letters go and only the ends stay
going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within another

lines of poetry are verse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' reads as an adjective or a routing instruction, but it is the verb meaning manage.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a project is to supervise and manage it, which is what one does when directing work.

clue.text: Back clipped on old passenger vehicle, wide say

indicators.note: with its back trimmed off, a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: ex- means former
a tram carries passengers on rails

explanation.surface: An old wide bus has had its rear end trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled too far from the batsman, and the run it gives away is counted as an extra; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes, no-balls and wides are all types of extras in cricket scoring, so a wide is an instance of the answer.

clue.text: Devastating blow for a dancer?

second meaning: one who does the Twist, the 1960s dance

explanation.surface: A crushing setback for a ballet performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' suggests a setback or punch, but it is wind blowing; the question mark covers the jokey second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is American slang for a tornado, and someone dancing the Twist could playfully be called one.

clue.text: Arenas, first of those in blue and lilac, nothing odd there!

the opening letter of the word
the second and fourth letters of the word

clue.text: Ultimately, abandonment justification for crime

explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country or sovereign, is among the gravest offences in law, so it is an example of a crime.

clue.text: Southern term for weapon

blocks.note: the abbreviation for southern
a term is a word

explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed hand-held arm used for cutting and thrusting, so it is one example of the class.

clue.text: Successful pop songs, those lined up for the Killers?

clue.text: Novel noted, ace story

clue.text: Weapon hidden in river well!
